question: How does false knowledge obscure reality and how is that obscuration removed?
premises: False knowledge is an unequaled darkness that produces defects of vision.
Because of it, even the pure appears as an abode of impurity.
When true vision removes the seal of defect caused by darkness, suspicion of impurity cannot arise.
inference: False knowledge distorts perception, making the pure seem impure; true vision removes this distortion, eliminating any doubt about purity.
plain_english: False knowledge is an unequaled darkness that produces defects of vision; due to its presence, even the pure appears as an abode of impurity. But when true vision, which is to be seen, removes the seal of defect born of that darkness, how can there be any suspicion of impurity there?
